title: Long-term survival group and risk cohorts in advanced, metastaticn non small cell lung cancer in Stage IVA and IVB
summary:
Lung cancer is one of the most common and serious types of cancer worldwide. Especially in advanced stages, treatment is often difficult and life expectancy may be limited. Over the past years, diagnostic and treatment options have changed and improved considerably.

The aim of this study is to investigate how different treatments and patient-related factors have influenced survival in people with advanced lung cancer. For this purpose, medical and treatment data from patients treated between 2010 and 2026 will be analyzed.

The study is retrospective and based on existing medical records and clinical documentation. No additional examinations or interventions will be performed.
conditions: Malignant neoplasm: Bronchus or lung, unspecified
